project.name: analyze
project.description: Django-style library loans and fees application with loans and fees modules, repositories, services, views and HTML templates.

tour.title: Project Overview: Loans Routing
tour.description: Start at the loans URL routes, the entry point for the plain-text API and HTML UI pages. Every request in the loans side of the app begins here and is handed to the views, giving a map of what the app exposes.

tour.title: Loan Views
tour.description: Building on the routes from Step 1, the views handle both the plain-text API and HTMX-aware UI pages. They delegate lending and returning to the loan application service instead of holding business logic themselves.
tour.languageLesson: Django views are plain functions taking a request and returning a response; ModelForm classes validate input and tie it to a model.

tour.title: Loan Service and Wiring
tour.description: The service layer implements lending, returning and listing against protocol interfaces, so it stays independent of Django. The composition root wires it to the Django repository and the system clock into one shared instance used by the views.
tour.languageLesson: Python typing.Protocol defines structural interfaces: any class with matching methods satisfies it, enabling dependency injection without inheritance.

tour.title: Data Model and Persistence
tour.description: The Loan model stores member, ISBN and dates, with a due date 14 days after lending. The repository implements the service's storage protocol using the ORM, with atomic creation and row-locked returns; the migration creates the table.

tour.title: Loan Templates
tour.description: Templates render the loan pages: a shared base, list and detail pages, and htmx partials such as the lend form and creation confirmation. HTMX lets forms swap fragments rather than reloading the page.

tour.title: Fees Routing and Views
tour.description: The fees app follows the same pattern as loans: routes lead to views that show late-fee details and handle payments, in both text and HTMX template variants.

tour.title: Fee Domain Logic
tour.description: The framework-free fee domain computes late fees (2-day grace, 25 cents per day, capped at 1000) and triggers payments. As with the loan service, it depends only on protocols declared here.

tour.title: Fee Adapters and Composition
tour.description: The fees composition root wires FeeApplication to the Django loan lookup, the clock reused from loans, and an HTTP payment gateway. The gateway posts charges without following redirects and maps transport errors to a domain failure.

tour.title: Fee Templates
tour.description: The fee pages show due date, days late and amount, then either the payment form or the result. The payment form and status partials are swapped via HTMX into #payment-status.
